Introduction gần như chép nguyên câu đề và không trả lời câu hỏi đồng ý hay không; Body 1 mở bằng “Technology providing”, Body 2 có “Although the improvement of technology” và “To evoke emotions ... digital images cannot convey” đều không thành chuỗi câu đúng. Conclusion lại thay “art galleries” bằng “historical object”. Bài chưa cho thấy khâu tự soát nghiêm túc: em cần viết lại toàn bài theo đúng lập trường không đồng ý, tự giải thích lỗi chủ ngữ–động từ và quan hệ từng câu rồi đối chiếu bản chữa.

paragraphs: Nowadays, some people claim that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary as computers allow people to view historical objects and works of art. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought: viewing an image cannot replace visiting a museum or gallery.

Admittedly, technology provides useful access to culture and history. First, high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms allow viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. Louvre museum is an example: art lovers around the world can join online tours to view works of art. This is especially useful for those who cannot afford to travel or have mobility issues; they can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, public museums and art galleries are still necessary. Although technology has improved, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Such a visit can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, seeing an old artefact up close may make its age and authenticity more vivid than an image can. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. By bringing visitors and local people together around that history, they can attract tourists and help people bond within the community.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that public museums and art galleries are still needed. Visits to these places provide a direct experience of history that technology cannot replace.

task.text:
Some people claim that public museums and art galleries will be no longer needed because people can see historical objects and works of art by using a computer.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
